Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy
Re: Creative Group Facilitator, Adolescent Mental Health

Dear Hiring Team,
I recently came across your Creative Group Facilitator opening and wanted to introduce myself. I understand the position may have been filled, but I would welcome consideration for this or future opportunities with Adolescent Wellness Academy.

My background brings together adolescent behavioral health support, recovery group facilitation, visual arts education, and fitness and wellness programming. 

At Family Center for Recovery, I supported adolescents and adults in structured treatment settings. At Futures Recovery Healthcare, I facilitated recovery support groups and helped alumni connect with resources and coping strategies. More recently, as an art teacher, I have designed creative activities that encourage confidence, expression, and engagement.

I am especially drawn to opportunities to help young people strengthen self-esteem and positive self-talk through art, movement, drama-inspired expression, and mindfulness. My approach values practical DBT-informed skills and creative activities as complements to the work of licensed treatment professionals.

I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience might support your programming. I have attached my resume for your consideration. 

Thank you for your time.

Warm regards, Jennifer Winston

candidates.cover_letter:
Sylvia De La Fuentes
Fresno, CA 93723 | The1stroundpick@gmail.com | 559-721-3608
 

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Team,
When I think about Support and the importance of support while someone fights to transform their life in addiction and mental health care, I know firsthand that when someone reaches out for support, that first human connection can change everything. I thrive in those exact moments of uncertainty, bringing warmth, clarity, and genuine advocacy to help individuals take that brave first step toward recovery.

In my current role as Lead Program Aide at Beloved Survivors, I manage client intakes, assess support needs, and track service referrals to connect individuals with vital community resources. Whether I am guiding someone through housing options or navigating employment applications, my priority is always making sure no one falls through the cracks. I understand that intake is not just about processing information; it is about building instant trust, listening deeply to a person's barriers and motivations, and walking alongside them with unwavering empathy.

My background spans both compassionate healthcare support and fast-paced operational execution. At Aetna as a Medicare Customer Service Representative, I handled high-volume inbound calls and outbound follow-ups, verified eligibility details, and maintained strict HIPAA compliance while supporting members through complex coverage questions. Additionally, my experience managing Salesforce CRM datasets and high-volume workflows at Oriental Motor taught me how to move quickly across multiple live queues, stay organized in a technology-enabled environment, and treat metrics as tools to improve service quality rather than sources of pressure.

I bring a consultative, outcomes-driven mindset combined with a deep, personal commitment to expanding access to high-quality care. I am ready to bring my energy, heart, and organizational ownership to Adolescent Wellness Academy.
 
Warmly,
Sylvia De La Fuentes

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear AWA People & Culture team,

I first came across Adolescent Wellness Academy through a job post. With a bit of research, I found it to be a beloved program that changed many young lives for the better. As a creative professional with a growing interest in psychology and a wish to work with the younger crowd, I made a note to myself: Reach out. With my help as a social media professional, we can share your story, multiply the healing impact and foster deeper connections with the local community.

As a digital storyteller, I have spent the last decade sharpening my tools, working in all facets of content production from concept development to polished delivery with a brand-tailored, mission-aligned strategic foundation. At Little’s Photography, I worked closely with hundreds of high-schoolers as a fine-art senior portrait photographer and photo editor, while producing an extensive promotional video library for the studio’s marketing initiatives. Our promos reached thousands of clients and led to a surge in the sales of photoshoot packages. I produced organic social content for the Columbia College Chicago Student Communications IG feed, and filmed interview-based documentaries that were showcased all across the university campus. With consistent hard-work as a freelancer, one of my long-time remote clients Emel Onur now has 47,500+ followers on her YouTube channel, compared to the 50 followers we started our journey with.

More recently, I helped establish an Instagram account that is dear to me. My teenage cousin Kağan has a rare form of epilepsy called Dravet Syndrome. Against all odds, he joined the Turkish national tennis team in the special needs category. My aunt was inspired to share their story, so we can build a community and reach those who can help Kağan access the treatment he needs. In the last 3 months, our engagement surged and we got more than 200,000 views. More importantly, we connected with people in very meaningful ways and networked with a foundation who wants to conduct research to find the right treatment. It makes me very happy to be able to have a positive effect on my family and community in Turkey from thousands of miles away.

What excites me the most about the prospect of joining your team is that I wholeheartedly share the aspiration to provide a safe space for teens, where they feel loved and cared for, so we water the seeds of healing for generations to come. I’d appreciate the chance to discuss how I can contribute to your mission. You can reach me at 561-409-6908 or idilmeric@hotmail.com. Thank you for your time—I look forward to hearing from you.

Warm regards,
Idil Meric

questionnaire.text: What experience do you have supporting adolescents, families, or individuals receiving behavioral health services?
questionnaire.response:
In 1998 I worked for a year in the Department of Psychiatry assisting with HIV/AIDS patients. I sat in meetings and took notes as the Psychiatrist conducted group sessions with patients.. I ran to get tissues, water or just hold patients who were emotionally distressed and needed a shoulder.  Later in 2005, I moved to Florida and had my daughter. I waited for my son and daughter to be eligible for preK and kindergarten so I could return to work.   I found work as an ESOL paraprofessional helping High School students from other countries learn to speak English.  During those 9 years I learned not only to help many Spanish speaking students learn English, but how to care for the ones who were emotionally distressed from various personal problems at home, I would accompany them to the social workers office and translate all the problems they were experiencing at home. I realized how much suffering and empathy was needed for my role.  I later left the position to care for my son who had a massive brain tumor and barely survived during the surgery.  As my son, progressed and I was forced to stay home.  I found work on line, which happened to be during COVID. 
   I recently went back to work part time as a Substitute teacher, and still find myself helping students of all ages with a variety of emotional issues.

These qualities are not only essential in our personal lives at home with our families, but when dealing with all people, especially those battling illnesses and obstacles!

I am excited to apply for the Clinic Director position leading the launch of Adolescent Wellness Academy’s first North Carolina clinic. As a licensed clinical social work and case management leader with more than 15 years of experience across behavioral health, healthcare, higher education, and community services, I offer the clinical supervision, operational leadership, and change-management experience needed to build a strong program from the ground up. AWA’s opportunity to create a focused, family-centered PHP/IOP clinic for adolescents is especially compelling to me because it combines direct clinical impact with the chance to shape culture, quality, and sustainable growth from day one.

Throughout my career, I have led complex case coordination, crisis response, care transitions, quality assurance, policy development, talent development, budgeting, and resource allocation. I have also provided clinical supervision and operational management while partnering with healthcare providers, hospital leaders, community agencies, and other stakeholders. These experiences would enable me to recruit and develop clinicians, establish clear clinical and documentation standards, guide level-of-care decisions, and build trusted relationships with families and referral partners across North Carolina.

I would bring a practical, outcomes-focused approach to launch execution: hiring and onboarding a cohesive team; creating a supportive environment for early-career clinicians; establishing reliable crisis, documentation, and quality-review processes; and using assessment findings and utilization trends to strengthen care delivery. My Master of Social Work and ongoing Doctor of Social Work studies in leadership further support my ability to connect evidence-informed clinical practice with disciplined operations and organizational growth.

AWA’s values—Dare to Grow, Contribute to the Whole, Choose Kindness, Spread Optimism, and Deliver Results—reflect how I strive to lead: with accountability, collaboration, compassion, and a clear commitment to excellent outcomes. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my clinical and operational leadership can help AWA launch a high-quality adolescent program and establish a strong foundation for long-term success in North Carolina.
Thank you for your consideration.

Sincerely,
Ty Matthews, LCSW, LISW-CP, DSW (C)

I’m prepared to bring this experience to benefit and eligibility verification, prior authorization and pre-certification workflows, concurrent and continued-stay reviews, and medical-necessity support. Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to discuss how my documentation review experience and behavioral health program background can contribute to your team.

Sincerely,
Lindsey Duran

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in joining the clinical team at Adolescent Wellness Academy. As a Florida Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern (RMHCI) with over 15 years of experience working with adolescents and young adults, I bring a unique combination of clinical training, youth development, experiential education, and a genuine passion for helping young people navigate life's challenges.

My journey into clinical mental health counseling grew naturally from my years working in Jewish education, teen engagement, summer camps, and experiential programming. Throughout these experiences, I discovered that some of the most meaningful growth opportunities happen when young people feel connected, supported, and empowered to explore who they are. This philosophy continues to shape my work as a therapist today.

I earned my Master of Science in Clinical Mental Health Counseling from Lynn University and currently provide individual therapy at Ellie Mental Health. These experiences strengthened my ability to engage clients with diverse clinical needs while balancing therapeutic connection, structured interventions, and individualized treatment goals.

My clinical approach is grounded in Adlerian theory, with an emphasis on belonging, social connection, encouragement, and understanding the patterns that shape how individuals see themselves and the world. I integrate Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT), Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT), Motivational Interviewing, and experiential interventions to create meaningful growth opportunities. I particularly enjoy incorporating creativity, active engagement, and play into the therapeutic process, recognizing that traditional talk therapy is not always the most effective way to connect with every adolescent.

What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy is your commitment to seeing beyond a teenager's presenting behaviors and recognizing the individual underneath. I strongly believe that adolescents deserve therapeutic spaces where they feel heard, respected, and valued, especially during some of their most challenging moments. Your collaborative, multidisciplinary treatment environment aligns with both my clinical philosophy and my longstanding commitment to supporting young people.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical skills, extensive experience in youth engagement, and enthusiasm for experiential therapeutic work to your team. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my background and approach could contribute to the meaningful work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

In Community,

Ross Glinkenhouse, MS, Registered Mental Health Counselor Intern

Dear AWA Academy Team,

I am so excited to apply for the opportunity to join AWA Academy’s IOP/PHP team working with adolescents. As a therapist who graduated in December 2025, I am eager to continue growing as a clinician in a setting that aligns with something I am truly passionate about: supporting children, adolescents, and their families. I am especially drawn to AWA Academy because of the impact your work has on the lives of children and families, and I would love to be part of that mission.

I currently work as an intake therapist for a virtual IOP program, where I work with both adults and children. I also have experience working in an inpatient psychiatric hospital with adults, where I facilitated group therapy and conducted intake assessments. These experiences have helped me build my clinical skills, connect with clients from different backgrounds, and better understand the importance of compassionate, individualized care.

Before becoming a therapist, I worked as a special education teacher with children on the autism spectrum. I genuinely love working with kids and helping them feel understood, supported, and empowered. My therapeutic approach incorporates concepts from ACT and DBT, and I am excited to continue building on these skills while gaining more experience in individual therapy. I would be genuinely excited to join AWA Academy and contribute to the meaningful work you do with children and families. Thank you for taking the time to consider my application. I would love the opportunity to connect and share more about my experience and enthusiasm for this role!

Hiring Team
Adolescent Wellness Academy
To whom it may concern,
I'm applying for the Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. For the past 11 months I've worked 2nd-shift admissions at OMT Addiction Treatment where I'm often the first person a client or family member reaches in the middle of a crisis. I’m also in recovery myself, I just surpassed 6 years clean—so I also have experience being on the other end.

* Document every contact accurately in Salesforce and follow HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 requirements
Working overnight has made me self-directed and dependable. I manage my own call flow, make sound judgment calls without a supervisor nearby, and follow through on every lead. Those habits transfer directly to a remote role, and I already have a quiet, reliable home office setup.
What draws me to your company is: the program model, level of care and online reviews. I want to work somewhere that puts the client's needs first while still running a strong admissions operation, and I'd welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your team's goals.
Thank you for your time and consideration.
Sincerely, Jeffrey Long

Emily Sestito, MS, CFLE

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator – Adolescent Mental Health & Substance Use Treatment

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. With a Master’s degree in Family Science, certification as a Certified Family Life Educator (CFLE), and extensive experience supporting adolescents, adults, and families in behavioral health settings, I bring a strong combination of clinical knowledge, compassionate communication, and organizational skills to this opportunity.

Throughout my professional career, I have worked with individuals experiencing mental health crises, substance use concerns, emotional dysregulation, trauma, and complex family challenges. My experience includes working within inpatient psychiatric treatment, partial hospitalization programs (PHP), intensive outpatient programs (IOP), and outpatient behavioral health services. These experiences have given me a thorough understanding of different levels of care, treatment coordination, clinical documentation, and the importance of connecting individuals with appropriate services.

In my work at Dover Behavioral Health System, I have supported adolescent and adult populations in a fast-paced psychiatric environment, facilitated therapeutic and psychoeducational groups, collaborated with multidisciplinary treatment teams, and helped individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances. My additional experience in outpatient behavioral health has strengthened my ability to establish rapport, recognize clinical needs, communicate effectively, and maintain accurate, confidential documentation.

What particularly attracts me to this position is the opportunity to serve as the first point of contact for individuals and families seeking treatment. I recognize that reaching out for behavioral health or substance use services often requires tremendous courage, particularly for parents concerned about their adolescents. I understand the importance of responding with patience, empathy, professionalism, and reassurance while helping callers understand their options and take meaningful steps toward receiving care.

Beyond my direct clinical experience, I bring strong administrative and technology skills, experience with electronic health records, familiarity with HIPAA requirements, and the ability to manage competing priorities independently. I am comfortable communicating by telephone, coordinating with treatment professionals, maintaining detailed records, and following through on time-sensitive responsibilities. I understand that successful admissions coordination requires not only compassion but also consistency, accuracy, and accountability to ensure individuals do not fall through the cracks.

I am particularly drawn to the missions of Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center because both organizations provide essential levels of care for individuals who need structured treatment and support. My professional background in family systems, adolescent development, mental health treatment, and crisis intervention would allow me to contribute meaningfully to your admissions team while helping prospective clients and families feel heard, respected, and supported.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my experience, dedication, and strong interpersonal skills to your growing organization. Thank you for considering my application. I look forward to discussing how my background aligns with your team's needs and how I can contribute to a positive admissions experience for every individual and family seeking care.

Sincerely,

Emily Sestito, MS, CFLE

My name is Cheseney Gall and I woiuld like to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator role. I am currently a licensed pharmacy technician with the State of Nebraska and I hold current certification through the Pharmacy Technician Certificiation Board. 

My experience outside of retail pharmacy includes hospital pharmacy, medication history technician, bulk packaging at the Nebraska Department of Corrections, pharmacy billing, prior authorizations, patient assistance, and clinical patient care coordinator. 

I have worked within healthcare my entire career with a focus on patient advocacy. I've worked with patients in group homes that live independently but need help with medication compliance. I provided medication therapy management (MTM) services to these clients. As a patient care coordinator, I was responsible for all client needs including housing assistance, disability paperwork, FMLA.

I have firsthand, lived experience with mental health and substance abuse recovery. I have survived cyclical patterns of abuse in my life and I work hard daily to regulate my emotions as I work each day to be the healthiest that I can be. I am a recovering alcoholic and have been sober since 4/19/22. I have been on medication for OCD/anxiety for 25+ years and I have two teenagers who have been diagnosed with Autism and ADHD. I want to be a resource to those needing services and to provide hope that circumstances do change.

I am very successful and most people in my professional career are unaware of the information that I provided in the last paragraph. I wanted to make my recovery a part of my life which is why I left pharmacy and moved to addiction medicine in 2024.

My most recent job was Intake Specialist at The Independence Center in Lincoln, Nebraska. We had Level 3.7 detox beds, short term residential, partial hospitalization and intensive outpatient programming. I ran the office and bridged the gap between counseling and clinical departments. I scheduled and ran a walk-in clinic offering substance abuse evaluations. I was responsible for PHP and IOP admissions, ensuring daily client attendance and participation along with communicating any patient behavioral concerns to interdisciplinary treatment team.

Before I got sober in 2022, I would drunk dial rehab facilities and admit to the person over the phone that I needed help. I had insurance at the time but I was nowhere near ready to stop drinking. I would get texts and voicemails from rehab facilities following up on my interest... even up to two years later. I was reaching out for help and that person on the phone was there. I have what it takes to be warm and welcoming over the phone while utilizing interviewing skills to determine what needs might exist. The intake process is a tricky balance of determining what services we can provide, what services are covered (insured), and how to best respond to each caller. Whether it's a person in crisis or a friend or family member that needs guidance. 

Behavioral health is my passion. I want to provide help and assitance to those needing it that are tough as hell to help. I've had people call me over the phone asking for help but are intoxicated and become verbal with me. No matter how that person may be presenting, even over the phone, they reached out because they need help. Their words may say one thing but their action was to have made a call. That's where admissions/intake begins.

I am working on earning my Certified Peer Support Specialist certification. I plan to take the exam in January 2027.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Scheduler position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a background in healthcare administration, legal client intake, scheduling, and customer service, I have developed the organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills necessary to support an efficient and compassionate admissions process.

Throughout my professional experience, I have coordinated appointments, conducted client intake interviews, managed high-volume phone communications, maintained confidential records, and ensured timely follow-up. Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, skills, and perspective could contribute to your admissions team and the important work being done at Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Ashlee Noeggerath

MacKenzie Paternostro
+1 (727) 858-5593
mpaternostro512@gmail.com

November 16, 2026

Hiring Manager
Adolescent Wellness Academy 

Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator Position

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With a bachelor’s degree focused in Criminal Justice and Social Work, professional experience in trauma-informed advocacy, and a strong background supporting individuals navigating complex and sensitive circumstances, I bring a combination of compassion, professionalism, and administrative experience that aligns closely with the responsibilities of this position.

In my current role as a Legal Advocate with Hope Villages of America, I work directly with survivors of domestic violence, including individuals experiencing significant emotional distress, safety concerns, and complex legal circumstances. My responsibilities require me to establish trust quickly, communicate with sensitivity, assess individual needs, coordinate referrals, explain complicated processes in understandable terms, and provide consistent support throughout a client’s experience. I understand that reaching out for help can be overwhelming, and I approach every interaction with patience, empathy, and the understanding that the way someone is treated during their first interaction can make a lasting difference. My experience has also strengthened my ability to manage sensitive information, maintain confidentiality, coordinate documentation, and communicate effectively with individuals from varying backgrounds. As a DCF-registered professional with victim-advocate privilege and specialized domestic violence training, I have developed a strong understanding of trauma-informed care, client privacy, safety planning, and the importance of meeting individuals where they are. These experiences have reinforced my commitment to creating supportive, judgment-free environments where individuals feel heard, respected, and empowered to take their next steps.

In addition to my advocacy experience, my previous position at the University of North Florida’s Student Accessibility Center provided me with valuable administrative and communication experience. I managed incoming calls from students, faculty, and families, directed inquiries to appropriate resources, coordinated testing logistics, maintained confidential records, and ensured accurate handling of sensitive documentation in accordance with FERPA requirements. These responsibilities strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to balance multiple priorities while maintaining professionalism and accuracy.

What particularly interests me about this opportunity is the ability to combine meaningful, person-centered work with the coordination and administrative responsibilities that help individuals access the care they need. I would welcome the opportunity to bring my background in crisis advocacy, client communication, resource coordination, and confidentiality to a team dedicated to helping adolescents and adults access behavioral health and substance use treatment. I would be grateful for the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to compassionate service could contribute to the success of your admissions team. Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the possibility of becoming part of your organization.

Sincerely,

MacKenzie Paternostro

Cover Letter
Meghan Martinez · (602)209-7642 · martinez.meghan.1991@gmail.com · Yuma, AZ
11/16/2026
Hiring Team Adolescent Wellness Academy / Principles Recovery Center
Re: Virtual Admissions Coordinator
Dear Hiring Team,
I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position. The first call someone makes to a treatment program is often one of the hardest moments of their life, and I would be honored to be the person who meets them with warmth, clarity, and a clear next step.
I should be upfront that I do not have direct professional experience in a behavioral health admissions role. What I do bring is a perspective that cannot be taught. Four years ago I struggled with alcohol, and I have been sober ever since. I understand the fear, the hesitation, and the vulnerability that come with reaching out for help, and I know how much it matters to be treated with patience and respect on that first call. I want to use that experience to make a real difference for the teens, adults, and families you serve.
My professional background has prepared me well for the day-to-day work of this role:
•	Phone presence and follow-through. Through my work in sales, including my most recent role at Brinks Home Security, I have spent years guiding people through important decisions, explaining complex services in plain language, and following up until every person has a clear answer. I am comfortable with high call volume and with building trust quickly.
•	Medical and insurance knowledge. I hold an active health insurance license and have worked in medical settings, including as a receptionist in optometry offices. I understand how to talk with patients about coverage, scheduling, and paperwork in a way that reduces stress.
•	Systems and documentation. I have used EMR systems such as Epic and am comfortable tracking details accurately and keeping patient information confidential and HIPAA-compliant.
•	Self-direction. I have worked on and off remotely since 2014, so I am very comfortable in that environment. I have also successfully managed my sales pipelines, medical collection client accounts, and follow-ups.
What draws me to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center is your commitment to meeting families and individuals where they are and guiding them from that first call to care. I would bring compassion, reliability, and a genuine understanding of what it takes to ask for help.
Thank you for considering my application. I would welcome the chance to talk about how I can support your admissions team and the people who reach out to you.
Sincerely,
Meghan Martinez

I am writing to express my interest in the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position specializing in Adolescent Mental Health and Substance Use. I am a highly motivated self-starter who takes initiative, demonstrates accountability, and works exceptionally well independently. candidates.cover_letter:
Valerie Vang

Adolescent Wellness Academy | Principles Recovery Center

Dear Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. What particularly drew me to this opportunity is the organization’s understanding that seeking treatment is often an emotional and difficult step for individuals and families. I appreciate AWA’s philosophy of treating people, not simply symptoms, and its commitment to creating an environment where individuals feel safe, supported, and understood. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to that mission by making each caller’s first interaction a compassionate and reassuring experience.

With a bachelor’s degree in Biology with a concentration in Health Science and a minor in Chemistry, alongside professional experience in behavioral health and healthcare administration, I bring a strong foundation in patient coordination, communication, and healthcare operations. My experience at Sagent Behavioral Health helped develop my understanding of behavioral healthcare environments, patient access, scheduling, and the importance of handling sensitive information with professionalism and discretion. In my subsequent roles with Summit Orthopedics and Minnesota Urology, I have continued strengthening my ability to manage high-volume phone interactions, coordinate appointments, communicate across departments, and navigate electronic healthcare systems.

I believe one of the most important aspects of this position is recognizing that an inquiry is never just another phone call. A parent reaching out about their teenager or an individual seeking support for substance use may be experiencing uncertainty, fear, or exhaustion. I would approach those conversations with patience, empathy, and professionalism while ensuring that callers receive clear information and appropriate next steps. I also understand that compassionate service must be supported by operational accuracy, consistent follow-through, proper documentation, and careful coordination with clinical and administrative teams.

My background working with healthcare platforms, including Allscripts TouchWorks, APM, PM/Veradigm, and other electronic healthcare systems, has strengthened my ability to adapt to technology-driven workflows while maintaining accurate records and protecting confidential patient information. I am comfortable learning new systems and processes, managing competing priorities, and maintaining a strong standard of communication in fast-paced healthcare environments.

I would be proud to bring my healthcare background, administrative experience, and patient-centered approach to your admissions team. More importantly, I would value the opportunity to contribute to an organization that recognizes how much a compassionate first interaction can matter in someone’s journey toward healing.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience and commitment to patient-centered service could contribute to Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center.

Sincerely,
Valerie Vang

I am applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position supporting adolescent mental health and substance use treatment. With a bachelor’s degree in Psychology, experience in behavioral health case management, and fluency in English and Spanish, I would bring compassionate communication, strong organizational skills, and a commitment to helping families access care.

As a Targeted Case Manager with Advanced Health Community Services since 2022, I support children, adolescents, and adults experiencing mental health challenges and complex barriers to treatment. My responsibilities include identifying service needs, coordinating referrals, communicating with providers, assisting with appointments, and following up with families to support continuity of care. This work requires accurate documentation, attention to confidentiality, and the ability to manage multiple priorities while remaining responsive to each family’s needs.

I have experience supporting adolescents and caregivers navigating depression, anxiety, trauma, behavioral challenges, and psychiatric hospitalizations. I understand how overwhelming seeking treatment can feel, and I approach families with patience, empathy, and clear explanations. My bilingual skills also allow me to communicate directly with Spanish-speaking families and help reduce language barriers.

I am eager to bring these transferable skills to admissions, helping families understand next steps, coordinating with clinical teams, and supporting a timely transition into appropriate treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to contribute to your team and help adolescents and their families feel supported from their first contact.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to discussing how my experience and dedication to accessible behavioral health care align with this position.

Sincerely,
Ledy Martinez

Dear Hiring Team,

I’m applying for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy and Principles Recovery Center. I enjoy being the person families can turn to when they know they need help and are trying to figure out where to start. This role brings together the work I’ve done in behavioral health intake, insurance verification, and supporting people seeking mental health and substance use treatment.

As a Bilingual Care Coordinator at Cartwheel Health, I was one of the first people students and families spoke with when starting services. I explained the intake process in English and Spanish, answered questions, coordinated appointments with clinicians and school teams, and followed up with families about next steps. In my current role as an Eligibility Specialist, I verify benefits, review documentation, and help families work through coverage issues that could delay care. Both roles have taught me how to keep multiple intakes moving remotely while giving each family the time and attention they need.

During my clinical internship at Catholic Charities in Trenton, I supported adolescents in the New Choices Program and adults in the Project Free intensive outpatient substance use program. I conducted intake assessments under supervision, facilitated groups, and coordinated referrals. That experience gave me a better understanding of what people may be going through when they make that first call and how much a calm conversation and a clear next step can help.

Thank you for considering my application. I’d welcome the opportunity to bring my bilingual communication skills, intake experience, and follow-through to your admissions team.

Sincerely,
Stephany Bhisham

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in this position. I hold a degree in Health Education, am currently pursuing a master’s degree in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, and have over three years of experience working as a substance use counselor. Throughout my career, I have worked with individuals from diverse backgrounds, providing support that considers each client’s unique needs, strengths, and challenges, in 1:1 and group counseling settings. 

In my current role, I manage a caseload of more than 50 clients while providing individualized counseling and education, coordinating care, facilitating group sessions, and maintaining accurate clinical documentation. I regularly incorporate cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) principles and realistic goal-setting into my work to help clients identify challenges, develop practical strategies, and make meaningful progress toward their goals. Managing multiple responsibilities has strengthened my organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to balance competing priorities while providing consistent, compassionate support.

One of the aspects of my work that I value most is building trusting relationships and creating an environment where individuals feel welcomed, heard, and supported. I believe that a safe, encouraging, and nonjudgmental environment helps people feel comfortable engaging with others, working through challenges, and building confidence in their abilities. I take pride in my strong client satisfaction ratings and in creating positive experiences through thoughtful communication, consistency, and reliable follow-through.


Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my experience, education, and commitment to supporting others align with your team’s needs.

Sincerely,

Jennifer Misko

I am excited to apply for the Virtual Admissions Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. With my current experience as a Behavioral Health Technician at Texas Recovery Center and my ongoing education in Counseling and Addiction Recovery Sciences at Texas Tech University, I believe I would bring both valuable experience and a genuine passion for helping individuals and families seeking treatment.

I understand how important it is for families to feel heard, respected, and supported when making decisions about mental health and substance use treatment. I would welcome the opportunity to help make that first step a positive and reassuring experience.

I am dependable, organized, comfortable working in demanding environments, and passionate about making a difference in the lives of others. I would be grateful for the opportunity to bring these qualities to your admissions team.

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my interest in the Primary Therapist position with Adolescent Wellness Academy in Mooresville, North Carolina. As a Licensed Clinical Social Worker Associate (LCSWA) with a Master of Social Work degree and three years of experience supporting children, adolescents, and families, I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to AWA's mission of providing compassionate, evidence-based mental health services to adolescents. I am particularly drawn to the opportunity to join the founding clinical team and help establish a supportive, collaborative, and client-centered therapeutic environment.

Throughout my professional experience, I have developed a strong foundation in family-centered treatment, crisis intervention, case management, treatment planning, and trauma-informed care. In my current role as a Family Centered Treatment Specialist with Pinnacle Family Services, I provide individualized treatment and case management services to children and families in home and community settings. I develop treatment plans, facilitate interventions, collaborate with community partners, and support families in navigating challenges while promoting stability, resilience, and improved outcomes. This experience has strengthened my ability to build therapeutic relationships, identify individual and family needs, and implement interventions that support meaningful behavioral and emotional change.

Previously, as a Family Advocate at Pat's Place Child Advocacy Center, I supported children and families navigating difficult and often traumatic circumstances. I provided emotional support, crisis intervention, resource coordination, and advocacy while collaborating with multidisciplinary professionals to prioritize child safety and family well-being. My school social work experience at Hawthorne Academy further strengthened my ability to recognize and address the emotional, behavioral, academic, and social needs of at-risk students while developing interventions and connecting families with appropriate resources.

I believe my background in child and family services provides a valuable foundation for working with adolescents experiencing anxiety, depression, trauma, behavioral challenges, and other mental health concerns. I am passionate about creating a therapeutic space where adolescents feel safe, understood, and empowered to develop healthy coping strategies and recognize their strengths. I also understand the importance of family involvement, interdisciplinary collaboration, individualized treatment planning, and consistent communication in supporting successful clinical outcomes.

I would welcome the opportunity to bring my clinical experience, dedication to family-centered care, and passion for adolescent mental health to Adolescent Wellness Academy. Being part of a new program would allow me to contribute not only to the care of adolescents and their families but also to the development of a positive clinical culture built on compassion, collaboration, and excellence.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I look forward to the opportunity to discuss how my qualifications, experience, and commitment to serving children and families would make me a valuable addition to AWA's founding clinical team.

Sincerely,

Abigail Cornele, MSW, LCSWA

candidates.cover_letter:
Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to express my interest in the Operations Manager position with Adolescent Wellness Academy as you prepare to open your first North Carolina clinic. What excites me most about this opportunity is the chance to be part of something that can make a genuine difference in the lives of young people and their families. Throughout my career, I have found the most rewarding part of my work is knowing that what I do has a meaningful impact on someone else's life. That is something I experienced firsthand at Shine Support Services, and it is something I hope to continue in my next role.

At Shine Support Services, I helped build the Supportive Employment Program from the ground up. I operated and developed workflows, internal procedures, training materials, participant resources, and documentation standards to help establish the foundation for daily operations. More importantly, I had the opportunity to work directly with individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities, support their goals, and build relationships with their families and community partners. I loved being able to see the difference that consistent support and encouragement could make in someone's confidence, independence, and everyday life. I taught a coping skills class that incorporated Dialectical Behavior Therapy (DBT) practices, giving participants the opportunity to learn and practice healthy coping strategies. Those experiences reminded me that meaningful progress is not always one big milestone. Sometimes it is the smaller moments of growth that make the work so worthwhile.

I also bring leadership and operational experience from Graphic Components, where I led the photopolymer department before being promoted to Project Manager. I coordinated departmental workflow, monitored quality, addressed production challenges, developed procedures and training documentation, and cross-trained employees and prospective hires. This experience strengthened my ability to organize competing priorities, support a team, solve problems, and create systems that help people do their jobs effectively.

My experience working with young people also extends to YPATC, a youth performing arts program in Florida, where my responsibilities ranged from scheduling appointments to teaching theater to children. I enjoyed being part of an environment where I could contribute both behind the scenes and directly to the experiences of young people. I have pursued the 40-hour Registered Behavior Technician (RBT) training coursework, further developing my understanding of behavioral support and different learning and support needs.

What draws me to AWA is the opportunity to bring these experiences together in a setting where the work has such an important purpose. I understand that a successful program depends on more than the services being offered. It also takes thoughtful organization, dependable staff, clear communication, consistent routines, and an environment where young people and their families feel supported. I would be excited to help build that foundation for AWA's North Carolina clinic.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I would welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, leadership, and passion for meaningful work could contribute to AWA's founding North Carolina team.

Sincerely,

Erica R. Warriner

Dear Adolescent Wellness Academy Hiring Team,

I am excited to apply for the Bilingual Virtual Program Coordinator position with Adolescent Wellness Academy. After reviewing the position and learning more about your organization’s commitment to supporting adolescent mental health, I believe my professional background as a Special Education Teacher and Case Manager would allow me to bring valuable experience and a meaningful perspective to your team.

Throughout my career in special education, I have worked closely with children and adolescents with a variety of developmental disabilities, behavioral challenges, communication differences, and individualized educational needs. My work has required me to look beyond academic progress and understand the individual as a whole, recognizing the importance of behavioral, emotional, social, and developmental support. I have developed a genuine appreciation for the important role that compassionate professionals play in helping individuals and families navigate challenging circumstances.

As a Special Education Teacher and Case Manager, I have experience managing caseloads, developing and monitoring IEPs, coordinating meetings, maintaining confidential records, documenting progress, communicating with families, and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams. I regularly work alongside administrators, parents, speech-language pathologists, occupational therapists, physical therapists, and other service providers to coordinate support and ensure individual needs are addressed. I also have CPI training and experience responding to behavioral challenges, recognizing safety concerns, and communicating important information to the appropriate professionals.

I believe these responsibilities have prepared me well for the coordination and administrative demands of this position. I understand the importance of accurate documentation, scheduling, timely communication, confidentiality, and ensuring that families and professionals have the information they need. I am comfortable managing multiple responsibilities, adapting to changing priorities, and maintaining a professional and compassionate approach when working with individuals and families.

I am also bilingual in English and Spanish. As a Puerto Rican professional, I understand the importance of communication that is both culturally respectful and accessible. I would be proud to use my Spanish-speaking abilities to help Spanish-speaking adolescents and families feel welcomed, understood, and supported when navigating behavioral health services. I believe that language should never be a barrier to a family feeling heard or accessing the support their child needs.

I am particularly drawn to this opportunity because it would allow me to continue doing work that I find meaningful while expanding my professional experience into the behavioral health field. My career in special education has taught me the importance of advocacy, patience, individualized support, and building trusting relationships with families. I would welcome the opportunity to bring those same qualities to a program dedicated to adolescent mental health and wellness.

I recognize that a successful program coordinator must be organized, dependable, attentive to detail, and able to communicate effectively with families and clinical professionals. These are skills I have developed throughout my career, and I would bring a strong sense of responsibility, compassion, and dedication to this position.

Thank you for considering my application. I would appreciate the opportunity to discuss how my experience as a Special Education Teacher and Case Manager, my bilingual abilities, and my commitment to supporting children and families could contribute to the mission of Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Johana Gonzalez

Dear Hiring Manager,

I am writing to express my sincere interest in the Admissions Counselor position at Adolescent Wellness Academy. With six years of experience in education as a Teacher's Assistant and Guidance Counselor, along with over five years of experience in healthcare, including mental health and substance use services, I bring a diverse professional background and a genuine passion for helping adolescents and families navigate life's challenges.

Throughout my career, I have developed a strong ability to build meaningful connections with individuals from all walks of life. My experience has taught me that effective guidance begins with understanding, compassion, and the ability to meet people where they are without judgment. Whether working with students, patients, or families, I believe every individual deserves to feel respected, heard, and valued. I approach every interaction with the understanding that I am not above the person seeking support; I am there to walk alongside them, offer guidance, and help them recognize their own potential.

My background in mental health and substance use services has further strengthened my ability to communicate with empathy, navigate sensitive situations, and establish trust with individuals experiencing vulnerable moments in their lives. My own personal experiences with loss and adversity have also shaped my perspective, deepening my appreciation for resilience, compassion, and the importance of having someone who genuinely believes in you. These experiences have reinforced my commitment to treating every individual with dignity rather than defining them by their circumstances.

My colleagues would describe me as ambitious, focused, reliable, and grounding. I take pride in my ability to bridge the gap between professionalism and relatability, creating connections that allow people to feel comfortable, supported, and understood. I believe my combined experience in education, healthcare, mental health, and substance use services gives me a unique perspective that aligns with the mission of supporting adolescents and their families through important and sometimes difficult transitions.

I am particularly drawn to Adolescent Wellness Academy because I value the opportunity to be part of an organization that prioritizes adolescent wellness, personal growth, and individualized support. I would be honored to bring my professional experience, personal perspective, and genuine dedication to helping others to your admissions team.

Thank you for your time and consideration. I welcome the opportunity to discuss how my experience, compassion, and commitment to serving others would make me a valuable addition to Adolescent Wellness Academy.

Sincerely,

Amanda Nieves-Rodriguez
